newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraqis go to streets to protest U.S. strikes - INA.
newsitem.headline: Iraqis go to streets to protest U.S. strikes - INA.

text.p: Angry Iraqis went to the streets on Tuesday to denounce U.S. missile strikes against their country, the official Iraqi News Agency (INA) said.
INA said demonstrations swept the capital Baghdad and other Iraqi cities to condemn the U.S. attack and show support for President Saddam Hussein's government.

The United States on Tuesday launched one of the biggest military strikes against Iraq since the Gulf War, firing 27 cruise missiles at targets in southern Iraq in response to Iraqi attacks in the north in support of a Kurdish faction fighting another Kurdish group.
Iraq said five people were killed and 19 wounded.

Saddam responded in a defiant speech by urging his air force and anit-aircraft gunners to attack United States and allied planes policing Western-imposed air exclusion zones in the south and north of his country.
